minutes.headline: Committee voted by roll call for the needs-based budget and an override request to the select board.
minutes.summary: The School Committee heard public comment on the budget and override, then reviewed the superintendent's updated budget versions. After a budget hearing, it voted by roll call for the needs-based (pink) budget and set an override request. It also took votes on the Student Opportunity Act plan, pulling a warrant article, sidewalk funding, and a Costa Rica trip.

A member's comments on last night's select board outcome, one-time ARPA money, and gamesmanship by the town side (speaking as committee member).
Thanks to parents; urged attendance at Town Meeting Saturday May 4th, 9 a.m.

Override ballot committee asked for concrete guidance on the override number.
Select board member urged a cross-department task force and long-term planning; supports needs-based budget.
School committee's philosophical role: advocate for schools vs work within town limits.
Asked committee for clear messaging that the need is real.
Remote select board member glad the override ask is higher.

votes.motion: Close the public portion of the budget hearing.
Approve the superintendent's needs-based (pink) budget at the amount stated.
Roll call vote on the pink needs-based 5.44% budget.
Propose an override to the select board as warrant article and ballot question for school funding above the town manager's budget.
Approve the Student Opportunity Act plan as presented.
Pull the warrant article for free cash for network security as funded by alternate means.
Approve reallocation of the sidewalk ARPA funding to the school department, sidewalks to come from Chapter 90.
Give final approval for the Costa Rica trip.

what_happened.line: After a budget hearing, the School Committee voted by roll call on the needs-based (pink) budget; the tally is not audible in the recording.
The committee moved to propose an override to the select board as a warrant article and ballot question; the result of that motion is not audible.
The chair and superintendent were authorized to adjust the override number before Tuesday if the town manager's figure changes.
The committee approved the Student Opportunity Act plan, pulled a free cash warrant article for network security, and moved sidewalk funding from ARPA to Chapter 90.
The Costa Rica trip received final approval, passing with one abstention.

why_it_matters: The override request is the school side's ask for money above the town manager's budget, and it is the kind of question that can reach residents as a ballot vote and a Town Meeting article.
The override amount was left adjustable after the meeting, so the figure residents are asked to vote on may differ from what was discussed here.
